title: Pachca MCP tool manifest
description: The contract a consumer validates before it boots. The server keeps no list of its own: it loads this file and serves exactly what is here. One tool stands on one API operation, except for the few that absorb a chain step; what a token may see is decided by the audience listings.

schema_version.description: Major changes when a consumer has to be updated.

generated_from.description: Which spec produced this file. The digest is content, not a timestamp, so the same spec always produces the same manifest.

instructions.description: The always-on block a model reads before its first call. Carries {placeholders} the server fills when a connection opens.

instruction_placeholders.description: What each placeholder in the instructions stands for. They belong to the caller and to the day, so the server fills them per connection: the date has to be known before the first call, and nothing else is in front of the model then.

cache.description: Listings are personal — what a token may see decides what comes back — so nothing here may be cached on a shared intermediary.

response_format.description: How a tool answers: the rules live here rather than in the server, so results do not differ per handler. Most entries are one line of text; the shape of the text half is a list of lines, and the cut of a long result carries its budget alongside the notice.

refusals.description: What an agent should do when a call is refused, by code.

compact_projections.description: The fields a compact card of each entity carries: the default for every read, full on request. A write answers with the whole record.

service_tools.description: Tools that are not one API operation: the documentation lookup, which reads nothing of the workspace, and the generic search and fetch pair one platform requires, which call several.

audiences.description: What each kind of token receives. The protocol allows a different listing per authorization, and a tool whose scope a role never gets is not shown at all.

jsonSchema.description: A JSON Schema without composition keywords: several clients silently drop a tool whose schema carries $ref, allOf, oneOf, anyOf or not.

additionalProperties.description: false on a tool's arguments; a schema where a value is a map — link previews by URL, errors by field.

annotations.description: What a client shows the person. Clients group tools by these and let one decision cover a group, so the flags decide what a single «always allow» opens.

operation.description: The one API operation this tool stands on.

scope.description: Read from x-requirements of the operation. Never written by hand, so a permission change in the spec cannot drift away from here. An operation the tool runs besides its own brings its scope to the argument that triggers it.

roles.description: Read from x-scope-roles of the spec.

outputSchema.description: The structured half of an answer: the response body as the API gives it, data and, for a list, meta. A read cuts each record to its compact card unless view is full; a write answers with the whole record. Nothing in it is required, so both fit.

entity.description: The entity a successful answer carries, as compact_projections names it. The runtime needs it to know which card to cut a read to.

request.description: How the arguments become the API request. They are flat for the model and the body is not, so every argument names its place.

in.description: upload: the server uploads each file and puts the result at `at`; server: the server's own argument, never sent to the API.

at.description: The dotted place in the body: message.content.

explode.description: false: a list in the query goes as one comma-separated value.

operations.description: upload: the operations the server runs to make each upload, in order — steps of the action rather than actions of their own.

scopes.description: upload: the scopes those operations need beyond the tool's own, read from the spec. Passing the argument without them is refused before the first step.

effect.description: server: what the runtime does with an argument the API has no field for. Declared rather than known by name, so a new argument of this kind is a new version of the package and not a change in the backend.

entity.description: Cut each record of the answer to the card of this entity unless the full view is asked for.

operation.description: Run this operation once the tool's own call succeeded.

at.description: The argument of that operation the value goes into.

scopes.description: The scopes that operation needs beyond the tool's own.

compat.description: Served only to clients that need it: the generic search and fetch pair exists because one platform's research mode requires that exact shape.

operations.description: The API operations the tool calls. Empty for the documentation lookup.

scopes.description: The scopes of those operations, read from the spec. The tool calls an operation only where the token holds its scope.

source.description: Where the answer comes from when the tool calls no API operation: a file shipped in the same package.

model_tokens.description: Roughly what this listing costs a model if a client loads it whole. Clients that fetch a schema when it is needed pay a fraction of it.
